description: Ability to use AI tools to structure, summarize, classify, and compare stakeholder needs and option inputs in a controlled analytical workflow.
historic work: Key Activities - Bullet 1: Supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using quantitative statistical data analysis methods, such as: data wrangling, validation, mining, and visualization (in R/RStudio, Python, SQL, Java, JavaScript or another software), as well as software development, application of machine/deep learning and artificial intelligence techniques for problem solving.
change to work: This activity is directly expanded from general analytical support to explicit support of AI-assisted needs identification and requirements analysis workflows. The existing reference to AI techniques becomes more operationalized: the analyst will not only apply tools for problem solving, but also validate AI-generated syntheses of stakeholder inputs, assess output quality, and help configure or use automated pipelines that support early-phase business analysis.
justification: The current activity mentions AI techniques broadly, but the update requires practical use of AI specifically for stakeholder-input synthesis, requirements analysis support, and validation of generated outputs rather than only conventional analytic tasks.

description: Ability to assess completeness, consistency, relevance, bias, and factual alignment of AI-produced summaries, categorizations, and draft materials.

The existing reference to AI techniques becomes more operationalized: the analyst will not only apply tools for problem solving, but also validate AI-generated syntheses of stakeholder inputs, assess output quality, and help configure or use automated pipelines that support early-phase business analysis.
justification: The update emphasizes minimizing manual intervention while preserving quality. This requires a stronger ability to test, verify, and challenge automated outputs than is explicitly required now.

description: Knowledge of how automated pipelines, prompt-driven systems, workflow orchestration, and human-in-the-loop controls support early statistical business process activities.

description: Ability to review AI-drafted summaries and recommendations for accuracy, context sensitivity, omissions, unsupported inferences, and appropriateness for audience and use.
historic work: Key Activities - Bullet 2: Analyses statistical data using established data management methods. Drafts summary analysis of qualitative and/or quantitative data and presents findings and recommendations to colleagues and/or team members.
change to work: This activity changes from primarily drafting summaries manually to reviewing and refining AI-assisted summaries and recommendations. The analyst will spend more effort confirming that machine-generated qualitative or mixed-method syntheses accurately reflect stakeholder needs and are suitable for downstream decision-making.
justification: The current duty covers summary analysis, but future work requires critical editorial and analytical oversight of machine-generated content.

description: Knowledge of standards for accuracy, traceability, readability, evidentiary support, and risk in AI-assisted analytical documentation.
historic work: Key Activities - Bullet 2: Analyses statistical data using established data management methods. Drafts summary analysis of qualitative and/or quantitative data and presents findings and recommendations to colleagues and/or team members.
change to work: This activity changes from primarily drafting summaries manually to reviewing and refining AI-assisted summaries and recommendations. The analyst will spend more effort confirming that machine-generated qualitative or mixed-method syntheses accurately reflect stakeholder needs and are suitable for downstream decision-making.
justification: The updated phase explicitly includes automated drafting of business case materials, requiring understanding of when generated content is sufficient and when escalation or revision is needed.

description: Ability to maintain records of source inputs, processing steps, model or tool usage, output versions, review decisions, and validation results.
historic work: Key Activities - Bullet 3: Organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies. Establishes and maintains work files.
change to work: This element is strongly affected because information organization and consolidation will increasingly be supported by automation. The analyst's role shifts toward structuring source inputs for automated processing, maintaining auditable records of AI inputs/outputs, and ensuring files, prompts, metadata, and validation notes are organized for reproducibility and accountability.
justification: The current activity includes file maintenance, but the future state requires more formal traceability across automated and AI-assisted processes.

development area: Metadata and input standardization for automation
description: Knowledge of how to structure, label, and manage data and text inputs so they can be reliably processed by automated and AI-enabled tools.
historic work: Key Activities - Bullet 3: Organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies. Establishes and maintains work files.
change to work: This element is strongly affected because information organization and consolidation will increasingly be supported by automation. The analyst's role shifts toward structuring source inputs for automated processing, maintaining auditable records of AI inputs/outputs, and ensuring files, prompts, metadata, and validation notes are organized for reproducibility and accountability.
justification: Automated synthesis depends on well-structured inputs and standardized metadata, which is not explicit in the current wording.

description: Ability to gather and format stakeholder inputs in a way that supports automated classification, synthesis, and later validation.
historic work: Key Activities - Bullet 4: Attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information and to optimize the business value of data.
change to work: Meeting participation becomes less focused on manual information capture and more focused on verifying AI-supported syntheses, clarifying ambiguous needs, and identifying context that automation may miss. The analyst may also support the capture of structured inputs that feed automated needs-identification systems.
justification: The update reduces manual needs-gathering effort but raises expectations for extracting contextual nuance and validating automated interpretations during consultations.

description: Ability to identify where stakeholder statements require human interpretation beyond automated summarization.
historic work: Key Activities - Bullet 4: Attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information and to optimize the business value of data.
change to work: Meeting participation becomes less focused on manual information capture and more focused on verifying AI-supported syntheses, clarifying ambiguous needs, and identifying context that automation may miss. The analyst may also support the capture of structured inputs that feed automated needs-identification systems.
justification: Automated summaries may miss nuance, so the analyst must better recognize ambiguity, tacit needs, and contextual qualifiers in discussions.

description: Ability to work within team processes where automated outputs are generated, reviewed, corrected, and approved across roles.
historic work: Key Activities - Bullet 5: Participates in project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis, and other unit activities.
change to work: Participation in teams will increasingly include collaboration on AI-enabled business process improvements, standard operating approaches for AI use, and human oversight practices for automated needs-analysis tasks.
justification: The update creates a need for junior staff to function effectively in mixed human-AI workflows within projects and working groups.

description: Knowledge of role-appropriate controls, review requirements, approval boundaries, and escalation expectations in AI-enabled analytical work.
historic work: Key Activities - Bullet 5: Participates in project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis, and other unit activities.
change to work: Participation in teams will increasingly include collaboration on AI-enabled business process improvements, standard operating approaches for AI use, and human oversight practices for automated needs-analysis tasks.
justification: Projects involving AI-supported needs specification require baseline understanding of governance and acceptable use expectations.

development area: Judgement in AI tool use and review
description: Ability to determine when automated methods are fit for purpose, when outputs are trustworthy, and when manual intervention or escalation is required.
historic work: Technical Activities - Bullet 1: Judgement is required to conduct non-routine data research, assess the relevance and reliability of the data sources and to organize and consolidate findings. Some judgement is required to select and apply established methods, as appropriate.
change to work: Judgement requirements increase in complexity. In addition to assessing source relevance and reliability, the analyst must assess reliability of AI-assisted interpretations and determine when established automated methods are appropriate versus when human-led review is necessary.
justification: The current judgement requirement focuses on sources and methods, but future work adds judgement about automated analytical outputs and tool suitability.

description: Knowledge of common AI issues such as hallucination, overgeneralization, prompt sensitivity, hidden bias, and false confidence.
historic work: Technical Activities - Bullet 1: Judgement is required to conduct non-routine data research, assess the relevance and reliability of the data sources and to organize and consolidate findings. Some judgement is required to select and apply established methods, as appropriate.
change to work: Judgement requirements increase in complexity. In addition to assessing source relevance and reliability, the analyst must assess reliability of AI-assisted interpretations and determine when established automated methods are appropriate versus when human-led review is necessary.
justification: This is a new knowledge area not fully captured by conventional data reliability assessment.

development area: Confidentiality and privacy risks in AI-assisted work
description: Knowledge of how sensitive information must be protected when using automated or AI-enabled tools, including approved-use boundaries and disclosure controls.
historic work: Technical Activities - Bullet 3: Judgement to discuss business information without divulging confidential information.
change to work: The confidentiality requirement becomes more complex because AI-enabled tools may create new disclosure, retention, and inappropriate-use risks when handling stakeholder information, internal planning content, or sensitive contextual materials during needs specification.
justification: The current requirement addresses confidentiality generally, but AI use introduces specific risks around data entry, tool selection, access, retention, and output sharing.

development area: Secure handling of data in AI environments
description: Ability to apply safe practices for preparing, redacting, submitting, storing, and sharing information used in AI-supported processes.

change to work: The confidentiality requirement becomes more complex because AI-enabled tools may create new disclosure, retention, and inappropriate-use risks when handling stakeholder information, internal planning content, or sensitive contextual materials during needs specification.
justification: Operational handling of information in AI workflows requires practical skill beyond general discretion.

development area: Preparation of source material for AI ingestion
description: Ability to clean, structure, tag, and normalize data or text sources so automated tools can process them accurately and consistently.
historic work: Technical Activities - Bullet 8: Conducts research and collects data from a variety of sources, aggregating it so that it provides valid and reliable data on which to perform quantitative, retrospective and predictive analysis that measures the impact of the Department’s programs to support evidence-based policy and program decisions.
change to work: Source collection and aggregation remain relevant but become more oriented to feeding automated needs-analysis processes with structured, quality-assured inputs. The analyst's contribution increasingly includes ensuring source comparability, labeling, and suitability for AI-supported synthesis and option analysis.
justification: The current activity emphasizes validity and reliability of data for analysis; the future state extends this to source readiness for automated and AI-supported synthesis.

development area: Source suitability criteria for AI-supported synthesis
description: Knowledge of which source characteristics affect automated extraction, summarization, comparability, and reliability.

description: Ability to use AI tools alongside data science methods to synthesize stakeholder feedback, categorize themes, and derive structured analytical outputs.

development area: Operational use of AI-enabled analytical tools

development area: Bias in generative and summarization systems
description: Knowledge of how AI systems can systematically misrepresent stakeholder input, overemphasize dominant perspectives, or omit minority needs.
historic work: Technical Activities - Bullet 12: Create and test data and mathematical models for bias, of particular importance in predictive and prescriptive analytics.
change to work: Bias testing remains relevant but broadens to include bias and distortion in AI-assisted stakeholder synthesis, requirements interpretation, and generated business case materials, not only predictive or prescriptive models.
justification: The current bias focus is model-centric; the update requires awareness that bias can also arise in generative and summarization systems used at the needs-specification stage.

development area: Bias review of AI-assisted needs analysis
description: Ability to examine AI-generated categorizations and summaries for representational bias, omission, skew, and unjustified prioritization.
historic work: Technical Activities - Bullet 12: Create and test data and mathematical models for bias, of particular importance in predictive and prescriptive analytics.
change to work: Bias testing remains relevant but broadens to include bias and distortion in AI-assisted stakeholder synthesis, requirements interpretation, and generated business case materials, not only predictive or prescriptive models.
justification: Practical oversight is needed to test and mitigate these issues in operational outputs.

development area: AI output validation for needs identification
description: Ability to assess the accuracy, relevance, consistency, and limitations of AI-generated summaries, classifications, and trend signals used to identify emerging statistical needs.
historic work: Key Activities - Bullet 1: Supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using quantitative statistical data analysis methods, such as: data wrangling, validation, mining, and visualization (in R/RStudio, Python, SQL, Java, JavaScript or another software), as well as software development, application of machine/deep learning and artificial intelligence techniques for problem solving.
change to work: This activity expands from using analytical tools mainly on study data to also using them on upstream needs-identification inputs. 'Validation' and AI-related techniques become more explicitly tied to reviewing automated classifications of user needs, feedback streams, and external benchmarking results. The analyst's contribution will include checking whether AI-generated needs summaries are accurate, relevant, and suitable for statistical follow-up.
justification: The current bullet references AI techniques broadly for problem solving, but does not explicitly require evaluation of AI outputs used in business-needs identification. The updated process requires the analyst to review, challenge, and refine automated signals before they shape downstream work.

development area: Interpretive analysis of automated needs signals
description: Ability to translate AI-detected patterns, anomalies, and clustered requests into clear analytical summaries with appropriate caveats, confidence statements, and operational implications.
historic work: Key Activities - Bullet 2: Analyses statistical data using established data management methods. Drafts summary analysis of qualitative and/or quantitative data and presents findings and recommendations to colleagues and/or team members.
change to work: The analyst's summary analysis will increasingly include synthesized needs evidence produced by automation, not only conventional statistical datasets. Recommendations will need to distinguish between strong and weak AI-detected signals, identify contextual caveats, and communicate confidence in the significance of emerging needs.
justification: The existing role supports summary analysis, but the updated process requires interpretation of machine-generated indicators and explaining their significance to others.

description: Ability to combine qualitative feedback, quantitative indicators, automated trend detection, and comparator information into coherent findings and recommendations.
